newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia car tariff report to be secret - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Australia car tariff report to be secret - newspaper.

text.p: The Productivity Commission's report on government assistance to the car industry is not to be released publicly until the federal government officially responded to it, the Adelaide Advertiser said on Monday.

The newspaper said it understood copies of the report would be provided only to the South Australian and Victorian premiers and the four major car manufacturers on the understanding they did not reveal the contents.

The commission was expected to miss today's deadline for the report's completion, due to a bigger than expected number of submissions and a lack of consensus between the three commissioners, the newspaper said.

The report was likely to be handed to the government on Wednesday, and the commission was believed to have remained divided, with the majority sticking by the draft plan to cut tariffs to five percent by 2004 from the current level of 22.5 percent. -- Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
